doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07

chapter: Touring Alabama and Florida, first New Orleans trips
title: Back in Pensacola with Mac: Florida tours and personnel
summary: After a year in Birmingham Billie toured Florida towns with Mac's six-piece band, including a Christmas back-and-forth run.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Well, anyway, after you left Buddy Petit and those guys, you went back to Birmingham, you said, with the Nighthaw. Yeah. How long did you stay there?
Well, I stayed there with them about...
I guess, I'm pretty near that... about a year. About a year. And, uh, pretty near about a year.
And then after you left the Nighthaw, what happened?

Then I, uh, went home. Going to Pensacola. Went to Pensacola. You played solo there, or you worked with bands? I worked with bands. That's when I started working with Mack Muramaker and them. I was in the town playing around. Tallahassee and Quincy and, um, Panama City, Florida. Appalachicola. Appalachicola, Florida. Oh, I had a good time on Appalachicola. Hey, at Jimmy Home. Appalachicola. And, um, all the through Florida. We've just been all around through this town like that, you know? Now, during the Christmas, during the holiday, I know, forget it. We played, uh, Quincy and Tallahassee. Backwards and four. All right, now, we played, uh, the night, we'll play a dance at Quincy. See? The night dance. Then we leave, after we play that dance, and come to Tallahassee and play a breakfast dance there in the morning. See? After we play that breakfast dance, right back to Quincy, I mean back to Quincy, you know? And play the evening dance. Till right there, that was during the Christmas time. Till that whole, we just see, saw back and forth like that. We didn't go no further. Right there, right there. We was gone for about a week, you see? I can see. And, uh, then we left and come on back to Pensacola, you know, for a rest, you know? Shut up, bro. Shut up. Shut up, bro. We played that dance, you know, during the holiday. We don't want you- We don't want you-
you shit a barking. We don't want you barking.
If you're gonna bark you gotta say your name one day.
But you see with that whistle blowing around here at 12 o'clock man he makes a noise. He do, he makes a noise, yeah. Ain't nobody like, where's my band? Well that's, that's a lot.
Who was in that band with you, in the match band?

George Morris, his trombone, trombone. And Sawyer, Sawyer, Sawyer, he was a drummer. And, let's see, I can't call this boy the Badger player. It's kind of like Wilbur or something, Wilbur or something like that, the way his name was. But he lives in Mobile, but he stayed over in Pensacola. And, myself, about a six piece band. Six piece band, I would have about six pieces. A clarinet player? Well we had saxophone play, had Leach out of Chicago. Leach, that's right. Leach out of Chicago, a boy played sax.
Where was George Morris from? Mobile.

Mobile. That's his home, that's his home in Mobile. George Morris from here. He's from here, from New Orleans. Yeah, he's from here. Did you know him today? He's from here, he's from here. George Morris, he's from here. George Morris come in with Mac, when Mac went over to Pensacola. George Morris from here. George Morris from here. I mean, in Louisiana. I don't know what, I don't know what he stayed in New Orleans, I don't know, I'll scratch the web, but he know actually from Louisiana. Yeah, right there.
